en_simple_draft.text: Śrīdhara explains that *dṛṣṭārtha* (the directly perceived) is what is grasped by the five pramāṇas; presumptive cognition (*arthāpatti*) of one fact from another such directly-perceived fact reduces to 'inference per contraries' (*viparīta-anumāna*). What is invariably concomitant with the inferendum is the *contradictory* of perception by another pramāṇa. He answers the Mīmāṃsaka who argues that 'inconsistency' alone (not invariable concomitance) drives arthāpatti: in fact the inconsistency is itself grounded in *vyāpti*, so arthāpatti is just *anumāna*. The *śrutārthāpatti* (presumption from verbal cognition — e.g. 'fat Devadatta does not eat by day' yields 'he eats at night') is likewise an 'inference upon inference': the verbal assertion infers fatness, fatness infers night-eating. Śrīdhara further argues that a word's function is only to express, not to remove inconsistencies in the world, so the cognition completed by the sentence does not 'need' another sentence — what needs supplementation is the *object*, and an object is supplied by an object, that is, by inference.

en_simple_draft.text: *Icchā* (desire) is the wish for an object one does not yet possess, either for oneself or for another ('may this be mine,' 'may this be his'). The varieties are not distinct guṇas, only varieties of icchā: *kāma* (the bare word *kāma*, without qualifier, denotes *maithuna-icchā*; when qualified — *svarga-kāma*, etc. — it stands for general desire), *kṣudhā* (desire for food), *sneha* (desire to experience an object again), *abhilāṣa* (desire for the not-near), *kāruṇya* (disinterested desire for relief of others' pain), *vairāgya* (desire to renounce after seeing fault), *upadhā* (desire to deceive), *bhāva* (the inferred, unexpressed inclination), and the various *kriyā-niyata* desires — *jigamiṣā* (wish-to-go), *jihīrṣā* (wish-to-take-away), etc. (Jha's printed English of the *sūtra* itself prints a lacuna at this point — 'Lust is desire................' — but the *Commentary* below, which is what this record carries, supplies *maithuna-icchā* explicitly.)

en_simple_draft.text: *Saṃskāra* (faculty / dispositional residue) is of three kinds: (1) *vega* (speed / impetus) — produced by *kriyā* in the five corporeal substances (*pṛthivī, ap, tejas, vāyu, manas*), aided by accessories like pushing and striking; not all motion produces vega, only motion thus aided. (2) *bhāvanā* — a *saṃskāra* of the *ātman* alone, the cause of *smṛti* and *pratyabhijñāna*. (3) *sthitisthāpaka* — elasticity, the disposition by which a bent bow or branch returns to its original shape. A long polemic against the Mīmāṃsaka *sphoṭa* doctrine is included: ordinary *saṃskāra*-driven *smṛti* of the letters suffices to deliver sentence-meaning; no extra *sphoṭa* entity is required.
